issues.title: Skip all-optional ConjunctionAnd table filters in the scan filter loop
issues.hypothesis: In q19 the lineitem scan (3.44s cumulative, about 85% of the query) carries a shipmode filter `optional: IN(..) AND optional: IN(..)`. Two optional pushdowns (filter_combiner.cpp:581 IN, and :659 OR-of-equals) on the same column get merged by TableFilterSet::PushFilter into a CONJUNCTION_AND. RowGroup::CheckZonemap (row_group.cpp:626) marks a filter always-true only when its top-level type is OPTIONAL_FILTER. So this AND stays active, and every 2048-row vector runs the column through ColumnData::Filter: a full decode of the shipmode Dictionary column, followed by FilterSelection calls on OptionalFilter children that do nothing. If the filter were skipped, the column would be fetched with Select on the few surviving rows (about 3 per vector in q19). Same-build A/B with `count WHERE l_quantity<2 AND l_shipinstruct=c AND l_shipmode IN(a,b)`, with and without an extra `(l_shipmode=a OR l_shipmode=b)` that produces the AND-of-optionals: scan 3.47s vs 3.03s, then 2.74s vs 2.25s cumulative (-13..-18%), with the same result rows. The upper FILTER operator re-checks the predicate anyway, so skipping it per row is correct.
issues.plan: In src/storage/table/row_group.cpp RowGroup::CheckZonemap: keep the existing prune check (CheckStatistics on the AND still prunes row groups). Add a static helper IsPurelyOptional(const TableFilter&). It returns true for a filter_type==OPTIONAL_FILTER that is NOT a SelectivityOptionalFilter (check with dynamic_cast<const SelectivityOptionalFilter*> == nullptr; that class can actually filter, e.g. the BF and min/max dynamic filters), and for a CONJUNCTION_AND whose children are all IsPurelyOptional (recursive). Leave the existing top-level OPTIONAL_FILTER branch unchanged. Add `else if (filter.filter_type == CONJUNCTION_AND && IsPurelyOptional(filter)) filters.SetFilterAlwaysTrue(i);`. SetFilterAlwaysTrue already clears column_has_filter, so the column is then fetched via Select (scan_state.cpp:101). Include duckdb/planner/filter/selectivity_optional_filter.hpp and conjunction_filter.hpp. Optionally also make TableFilterSet::PushFilter (src/planner/table_filter.cpp) skip pushing an OptionalFilter whose child equals an existing optional child, to dedupe; keep that secondary. Verify with EXPLAIN ANALYZE of q19 (the lineitem scan should drop clearly) and with bench.
issues.expected_gain: q19 -8..-15% (lineitem scan is about 85% of time; the microbench shows -13..-18% scan time)
issues.generality: Any scan where two or more optional (zonemap-only) pushdowns land on the same column: IN lists combined with OR-of-equals, IN plus top-N filters, or derived OR filters from JoinDependentFilterRule. Today these needlessly force a full decode of the column per vector. No query should get slower: the skipped filter was a no-op per row. SelectivityOptionalFilter (BF/min-max dynamic filters) is excluded, so selective dynamic filtering is untouched.
issues.risk: Low. One branch in CheckZonemap. The main hazard is accidentally treating a SelectivityOptionalFilter as purely optional, which would disable BF filtering (performance only, still correct because the join re-checks). Correctness is preserved because optional filters are always re-evaluated by the FILTER above the scan.
